title: Choosing Supervised Post-Processing for Frozen Person Detectors: Information, Object Changes, and Complete Cost
abstract: arXiv:2611.24003v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A frozen detector computes hypotheses that can support better final outputs through supervised post-processing. Choosing a readout requires knowing which available information improves detection and what its processing costs. We compare candidate scores, class distributions, geometry, native-set summaries and adapted neighborhood meta classification under common candidate, supervision and operating-point conditions. On 320 held-out CrowdHuman images, adding native-set context to a 97-dimensional readout yields 275 more matches and 96 more unmatched predictions. On a separate 319-image cohort, Full100 matches 6004 objects,versus 5848 for source-selected raw WBF and 6002 for a MetaDetect-style adaptation. Its gain over raw contains 300 added and 144 lost discoveries. After execution-equivalent optimization, Full100 and the meta-statistics readout both take approximately 95 ms per complete warm request on a fixed 64-image workload. Source

translated_title: 为冻结行人检测器选择监督后处理：信息、目标变化与完整成本
translated_abstract: 冻结检测器所计算的假设可以通过监督后处理来支持更好的最终输出。选择读出方案需要了解哪些可用信息能够改进检测，以及其处理成本是多少。我们在共同的候选、监督和工作点条件下，比较了候选分数、类别分布、几何信息、原生集合摘要以及自适应邻域元分类。在320张保留的CrowdHuman图像上，向97维读出中添加原生集合上下文可带来275个额外的匹配和96个额外的未匹配预测。在另一个319张图像的独立队列上，Full100匹配了6004个目标，而基于源选择的原始WBF匹配5848个，MetaDetect风格的自适应方法匹配6002个。相对于原始方法，其增益包含300个新增发现和144个丢失的发现。在执行等效优化之后，在固定的64张图像工作负载上，Full100和元统计读出每次完整的热请求大约需要95毫秒。
tldr: 该论文在统一的候选、监督与工作点条件下系统比较了冻结行人检测器的多种监督后处理读出方案，发现包含原生集合上下文的Full100读出在计算成本相当（约95毫秒/请求）的情况下，比原始WBF和MetaDetect式自适应方法多匹配数百个目标。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically compares supervised post-processing readouts for frozen person detectors under common candidate, supervision, and operating-point conditions, showing that the Full100 readout with native-set context matches substantially more objects than raw WBF and MetaDetect-style adaptation at comparable computational cost (~95 ms per warm request).
